title: Open-weight models beat the closed frontier on legal tasks with Harvey
authors: Jonathon Liu, Xavier Morris, Will Rankin, Aaron Ellis-Bloor, Matthew Blau, Albert Lee
gist: Harvey and a provider post-trained four recent open models on agentic legal work and scored them on Harvey's benchmark, where a task passes only if every criterion is met. All four rose by 11 to 21 points. One, at 30.3%, passed the best closed model at 27.1%; the other three stayed below it but above two other closed models. Coding scores held.
changes: Tuning turns out to be a treadmill that still pays. Harvey's August tune of an older model, at 19.7%, was passed by an untuned general model within three months. Re-tuning newer bases took the lead back. For a provider, post-training is work that repeats with every base model, like a drafter or an engine.
caveats: Run by the provider and the customer on the customer's own benchmark. Closed-model scores came from a slightly different harness, reproduced within a point for one model. No cost per task, no training compute and no held-out split for the main benchmark are given. The headline says open models beat the closed frontier; one of four tuned models did.
